result.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly model-generated responses, motivating larger rollout batches and square-root learning-rate scaling. Reported to approximately preserve progress per sample with one optimizer step per rollout, this rule is less understood in practical multi-step training. We develop a two-clock framework that separates the samples needed to make progress from those consumed before collapse. Under a local quadratic model, the square-root rule preserves first-order drift per sample but not progress: larger batches take fewer, longer updates and lose more to curvature, yielding a learning-rate-dependent critical batch beyond which sample efficiency degrades. A drift-threshold hypothesis predicts a complementary failure clock whose sample count remains approximately invariant along the square-root rule. Controlled GRPO experiments on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B across a $16\times$ batch range support both predictions. Ratio clipping delays failure, especially for larger batches, but the progress gap persists without it. Widening the clip trades stability for a transient speed gain. The progress gap reappears on another dataset, a general-purpose checkpoint, and a 7B model. Finally, we use the two-clock framework to derive a simple multi-step RLVR schedule: start below the critical batch and switch to a larger batch before failure. Our code is available at: https://github.com/WinstonLiyt/two-clocks-rlvr.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 two-clock 框架，把 RLVR 中「取得进展所需样本」与「崩溃前消耗样本」分开，在局部二次模型下推导出 critical batch 与失效时钟，并用 Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B 的 GRPO 实验在 16 倍 batch 范围内验证，进而给出一套多步 batch 调度。
AI.relevance_reason: LVR 常用 RLVR 类目标训练，其 critical batch、平方根缩放与双时钟分析可供核查：rollout 规模与更新步长如何影响 latent 推理训练的样本效率与失效时机；但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
